title: Soviet industrial/office analog wall clock — «Стрела» family round metal-rim secondary (slave) clock, ВЧС-type; in-game fictional brand «ЧАСОЗБОР»
era: USSR, 1950s–1980s (Strela secondary clocks from the 1950s, 1st Moscow Watch Factory; bakelite/metal factory variants documented through the 1980s)

sources.note: Strela factory wall clock, 1970s: 28x28 cm, depth 7 cm, 1.5 kg; 'white bakelite frame, an iron dial and a clear glass cover'; slave clock converted to AA battery.
Larger Strela factory wall clock, 1980s: diameter 35 cm, depth 8 cm, 1.5 kg. Corroborated by 1stdibs id-f_28167302.

'Soviet Clock ARROW STRELA. USSR electric wall controllable Watch. Original' — width 282 mm; 'the secondary clock operates from a clock station, which issues pulses'. Bot-gated; captured via search excerpt.
'Strela VChS1 — used in institutions and enterprises of various profiles in the USSR' (ВЧС-1). Search excerpt.
«Настенные часы вторичные „Стрела“ для установок единого времени учреждений. СССР, Первый Московский часовой завод, 1950-е гг. Дерево, стекло, металл.»
Вторичные часы: +24 V DC minute pulses, polarity alternating each minute; 'простой шаговый двигатель и несколько шестеренок'; ubiquitous in Soviet enterprises.
'Управление… минутными импульсами чередующейся полярности по простой двухпроводной линии'.
Corroborates alternating-polarity minute pulses (H-bridge stepper drive).
ВЧС-03/ВЧС-04 successor line: dial diameters 285/320/330 and 350/400 mm; 'Корпус – алюминий…'; 'Стрелки – алюминий и магниилум'; ГОСТ 27576-87.
ВЧС-03: 'Корпус – алюминий, окрашенный эмалью'; standard version 24 V; ГОСТ 27752-88.
'ВЧС-03/03 285 мм' — 285 mm as a standard dial size of the ВЧС line.
Hammered enamel («молотковая эмаль») case paint + metal cap over mechanism; convex glass on some models. WEAK: Cloudflare-gated, captured via search excerpts only.

case_outer_diameter_mm.note: Round metal-cased Strela secondary clock, listed width 282 mm. Family spans ~280 (pamono-strela-1970s) to 350 mm (pamono-strela-1980s).

case_depth_mm.note: Depth of the Ø280 mm Strela sibling (28x28x7 cm). Depth of the 282 mm metal version itself not stated — see needs[].

weight_kg.note: Both Pamono Strela listings state 1.5 kg.

dial_diameter_standard_mm.note: Smallest standard DIAL diameter of the ВЧС-03 line; the vintage 282 mm figure is the CASE — visible dial opening is smaller (rim width unsourced, see needs[]).

case_material.value: stamped metal; successor line: aluminium painted with enamel

finish_hammered_enamel.value: grey hammered enamel («молотковая эмаль») + metal cap over rear mechanism
finish_hammered_enamel.note: WEAK provenance — excerpt-only capture of a gated page.

glass_cover.value: clear glass cover over the dial
glass_cover.note: Domed/convex glass attested only by the weak allaudio source.

movement_type.value: secondary (slave) clock: stepping motor + reduction gears behind a rear mechanism cap, no local timekeeping
movement_type.note: Hands advance one minute per pulse — the in-game metaphor: hands are driven by the central game._worldClock, never by the prop itself.

pulse_voltage_v.note: +24 V DC minute pulses from the primary clock station.

pulse_scheme.value: minute pulses of alternating polarity over a simple two-wire line entering the back of the case

no_face_controls.value: no winding or setting elements on the face — drive is entirely external

maker.value: Первый Московский часовой завод, brand «Стрела» (in-game fictionalised as «ЧАСОЗБОР»)
maker.note: Owner picked the fictional wordmark; dial layout follows the Стрела reference photo.

deployment.value: unified-time installations: factories, schools, stations, offices

gost_standard.note: Standards governing the ВЧС secondary-clock line.
